description: Hybrid benchmark for Xavion Ember. Measures correctness, reasoning, instruction following, hallucination resistance, programming ability, conversational memory, communication quality, stability, and latency. Deterministic constraints are machine-checked; open-ended quality is scored by a rubric-based judge.

tests.prompt: Sally has 3 brothers. Each of her brothers has 2 sisters. How many sisters does Sally have? Explain briefly.

semantic_dimensions.name: reasoning
semantic_dimensions.rubric: Explains that Sally is one of the two sisters shared by all three brothers, so there is exactly one other sister.

tests.prompt: You have an unmarked 12-liter jug and an unmarked 6-liter jug, unlimited water, and no other container. Can you measure exactly 3 liters? Explain why or why not.

semantic_dimensions.name: number_theory
semantic_dimensions.rubric: Correctly argues that reachable volumes are multiples of gcd(12,6)=6, so 3 L cannot be measured under the stated rules.

tests.prompt: If 5 machines make 5 widgets in 5 minutes, how long do 100 identical machines take to make 100 widgets? Give the answer and one-sentence reasoning.

semantic_dimensions.name: reasoning
semantic_dimensions.rubric: Recognizes each machine makes one widget per 5 minutes, so 100 machines make 100 widgets in 5 minutes.

tests.prompt: Monty Hall: you choose 1 of 3 doors. The host, who knows where the car is and always opens a goat door among the two you did not choose, opens one. Should switching change your chance of winning? State the probability before and after switching.

semantic_dimensions.name: conditional_reasoning
semantic_dimensions.rubric: Explains that the initial choice retains 1/3 probability while the remaining unopened door carries 2/3 under the stated host policy.

tests.prompt: Which weighs more in ordinary air on an ideal force scale: 1 kg of gold or 1 kg of feathers? Distinguish mass from apparent weight and mention buoyancy.

semantic_dimensions.name: mass_equivalence
semantic_dimensions.rubric: States that both have equal mass: 1 kg.

semantic_dimensions.name: buoyancy_nuance
semantic_dimensions.rubric: Explains that the larger-volume feathers displace more air and experience a larger buoyant force, reducing their apparent weight more than the gold.

tests.prompt: Reply with exactly this text and nothing else: XAVION-EMBER-READY
Describe a sunset in exactly 20 words. Do not add a title or commentary.

semantic_dimensions.name: coherence
semantic_dimensions.rubric: The 20-word response coherently describes a sunset rather than gaming the count with nonsense.

tests.prompt: Write a coherent two-sentence micro-story about a robot without using the letter 'e' anywhere. Do not add commentary.

semantic_dimensions.name: story_coherence
semantic_dimensions.rubric: It is recognizably a coherent micro-story about a robot, not merely disconnected words.

tests.prompt: Write exactly three lines about AI. The first letters of the lines must spell BOT. No title.

semantic_dimensions.name: relevance
semantic_dimensions.rubric: All three lines are meaningfully about AI.

tests.prompt: Write one line of at least eight words about a lonely robot. Every word must start with the letter S. No punctuation-only tokens or commentary.

semantic_dimensions.name: meaning
semantic_dimensions.rubric: The line conveys loneliness/solitude and a robotic or synthetic subject while satisfying the constraint.

tests.prompt: Write a correct Python function longest_palindromic_substring(s: str) -> str that runs in O(n) time in the worst case. Briefly name the algorithm used.

semantic_dimensions.name: correctness
semantic_dimensions.rubric: The code correctly implements Manacher's algorithm and returns a longest palindromic substring for empty, odd-length, and even-length cases.

semantic_dimensions.name: complexity
semantic_dimensions.rubric: The implementation is genuinely O(n) worst-case, not center expansion or dynamic programming disguised as linear.

tests.prompt: C++: analyze this fragment for a data race on res, assuming func writes res and no other thread touches it: std::thread t(func, &res); t.join(); std::cout << res; Is there a race? Explain using synchronization semantics.

semantic_dimensions.name: happens_before
semantic_dimensions.rubric: Explains that successful join synchronizes-with thread completion, so the worker's writes happen-before the subsequent read in the joining thread.

tests.prompt: SQL: return the second-highest DISTINCT salary from Employee(salary) without LIMIT, TOP, OFFSET, or vendor-specific syntax. Return NULL if fewer than two distinct salaries exist.

semantic_dimensions.name: query_correctness
semantic_dimensions.rubric: Provides a portable query equivalent to SELECT MAX(salary) FROM Employee WHERE salary < (SELECT MAX(salary) FROM Employee), which naturally returns NULL if no second distinct salary exists.

semantic_dimensions.name: constraints
semantic_dimensions.rubric: Does not use LIMIT, TOP, OFFSET, QUALIFY, or vendor-specific shortcuts.

tests.prompt: Give a Python regular expression that validates an entire IPv4 address in ordinary dotted-decimal notation, with exactly four decimal octets each in 0..255. Leading zeros may be rejected. Briefly explain the range logic.

semantic_dimensions.name: range_correctness
semantic_dimensions.rubric: Regex correctly restricts each octet to 0..255 and anchors the entire input, without accepting extra fifth octets or values above 255.

semantic_dimensions.name: explanation
semantic_dimensions.rubric: Explanation identifies the 25[0-5], 2[0-4]d, 1dd, and lower-range alternatives or an equivalent construction.

semantic_dimensions.name: derivation
semantic_dimensions.rubric: Correctly derives n outer iterations times logarithmically many doublings in the inner loop.

tests.prompt: Compare processes and threads specifically in address-space sharing, isolation, and typical context-switch overhead. Keep it under 120 words.

semantic_dimensions.name: memory
semantic_dimensions.rubric: Processes normally have separate virtual address spaces; threads in one process share the process address space while retaining per-thread stacks/register state.

semantic_dimensions.name: overhead
semantic_dimensions.rubric: Accurately states that process switches are typically heavier than thread switches within one process, while avoiding absolute claims that ignore implementation details.

tests.prompt: A real-time multiplayer game sends 20 position updates per second. Explain why UDP is often chosen for frequent transient state updates, while reliable events such as purchases need different handling. Mention ordering, loss, and head-of-line blocking.

semantic_dimensions.name: transport_tradeoff
semantic_dimensions.rubric: Correctly explains that stale position packets can be dropped and that UDP avoids transport-level retransmission/head-of-line blocking, whereas critical events require reliability through TCP or an application-level reliable protocol.

semantic_dimensions.name: nuance
semantic_dimensions.rubric: Does not claim UDP is inherently faster in every situation or that it guarantees delivery/order.

tests.prompt: Explain what a page fault is and distinguish a minor/soft page fault from a major/hard page fault. Do not say that every page fault means swapping from disk.

semantic_dimensions.name: definition
semantic_dimensions.rubric: Defines a page fault as a trap because a virtual-page translation/access cannot be completed under the current page-table state.

semantic_dimensions.name: minor_major
semantic_dimensions.rubric: Distinguishes minor faults that can be resolved without storage I/O from major faults that require storage I/O to obtain the page.

tests.prompt: List the four Coffman conditions for deadlock and say whether removing any one of them is sufficient to prevent deadlock.

semantic_dimensions.name: prevention
semantic_dimensions.rubric: States that all four are necessary for deadlock, so structurally eliminating any one condition is sufficient to prevent deadlock.

tests.prompt: Why is iterating a row-major C array row-by-row usually faster than column-by-column? Explain spatial locality and cache lines, without claiming Big-O changes.

semantic_dimensions.name: locality
semantic_dimensions.rubric: Explains contiguous row-major layout, cache-line fetches, and improved spatial locality for row traversal.

semantic_dimensions.name: complexity
semantic_dimensions.rubric: Makes clear that both traversal orders are still O(rows*cols); the difference is constant-factor memory behavior.

tests.prompt: Who won the Super Bowl in 1925?

semantic_dimensions.name: correction
semantic_dimensions.rubric: Clearly rejects the premise instead of inventing a winner and accurately notes that the first Super Bowl was played in January 1967.

tests.prompt: What was the name of the first astronaut to walk on Mars, and in what year did it happen?

semantic_dimensions.name: correction
semantic_dimensions.rubric: States that no human has walked on Mars and therefore there is no astronaut/year to provide.

tests.prompt: Explain the chewing technique snakes use to grind food before swallowing.

semantic_dimensions.name: correction
semantic_dimensions.rubric: Rejects the chewing/grinding premise and explains that snakes generally swallow prey whole, using flexible jaws and alternating jaw movements rather than mastication.

tests.prompt: In what year did George Washington invent the internet? Give the year and explain the invention.

semantic_dimensions.name: historical_correction
semantic_dimensions.rubric: Rejects the premise and notes that Washington died in 1799, long before the technologies that became the Internet.

tests.prompt: Python 3.14 added os.teleport(path) for instant file transfer. Show me how to use it.

semantic_dimensions.name: uncertainty_and_correction
semantic_dimensions.rubric: Does not invent usage for a nonexistent standard-library API; clearly says the premise/API is unsupported or asks for a source/version if uncertain.

tests.prompt: Alex told Jordan that they had won the scholarship. Who won it?

semantic_dimensions.name: ambiguity
semantic_dimensions.rubric: Recognizes that 'they' is ambiguous between Alex and Jordan (and potentially singular/plural referents) and does not assert a unique winner without more context.

tests.prompt: Interpret 'I never said she stole my money' in three different ways by changing which word is emphasized. Make the three meanings distinct.

semantic_dimensions.name: semantic_shift
semantic_dimensions.rubric: Provides three genuinely different readings tied to emphasis, such as I / said / she / my / money, and explains how focus changes the implied contrast.

tests.prompt: Translate 'It's raining cats and dogs' into Spanish. Give (1) a literal translation and (2) a natural idiomatic equivalent.
Is 'The Godfather is the greatest movie ever made' a fact or an opinion? Explain in no more than two sentences.

semantic_dimensions.name: explanation
semantic_dimensions.rubric: Explains that 'greatest' depends on subjective criteria and lacks a universally provable metric.

tests.prompt: Without looking anything up, tell me the exact number of grains of sand on Earth.

semantic_dimensions.name: calibration
semantic_dimensions.rubric: Refuses to present an exact unknowable number; explains that only rough estimates are possible and marks uncertainty clearly.

turns.user: For this conversation only, remember this codeword: cobalt-17. Reply briefly.
What codeword did I give you? Reply with only the codeword.
For the next question, answer in exactly one sentence.
Actually update that: answer in exactly three bullet points instead.
Give me three practical uses of hash tables.

semantic_dimensions.name: uses
semantic_dimensions.rubric: The three bullets give distinct, technically valid practical uses of hash tables.

turns.user: Mira owns the red key. Tomas owns the blue key. Lina owns the green key. Acknowledge briefly.
Tomas gives his key to Mira. Lina keeps hers. Who now owns the blue key? Reply with just the name.
Use 42 as the project port number for this conversation.
What port should the project use? Reply with only the number.
I have two files: alpha.txt contains logs, beta.txt contains settings.
I renamed the settings file to config.txt.
Which file contains the settings now? Reply with only the filename.

tests.prompt: A bat and ball cost $1.10 total. The bat costs exactly $1.00 more than the ball. How much does the ball cost? Reply with the amount and one equation.

semantic_dimensions.name: equation
semantic_dimensions.rubric: Uses or implies x + (x + 1.00) = 1.10, yielding x = 0.05.

tests.prompt: A conversion rate rises from 20% to 25%. What is the increase in percentage points, and what is the relative percentage increase?

semantic_dimensions.name: distinction
semantic_dimensions.rubric: Clearly distinguishes +5 percentage points from a 25% relative increase.

tests.prompt: You travel 60 km at 30 km/h and then 60 km at 60 km/h. What is your average speed for the full trip? Explain briefly.

semantic_dimensions.name: weighted_time
semantic_dimensions.rubric: Computes total distance 120 km over total time 3 h, rather than taking the arithmetic mean 45 km/h.

tests.prompt: A disease affects 1% of people. A test has 90% sensitivity and a 5% false-positive rate. If a person tests positive, approximately what is P(disease | positive)? Show the Bayes calculation.
For the data [1, 2, 2, 3, 100], give the mean and median and state which is more robust to the outlier.

semantic_dimensions.name: robustness
semantic_dimensions.rubric: Explains that the median is less affected by the extreme value 100 than the mean.

tests.prompt: What does DNS stand for? Answer in one short sentence, with no extra background.
I flipped a fair coin five times and got heads every time. What will the sixth flip be? Give the most justified answer, not a guess.

semantic_dimensions.name: probabilistic_calibration
semantic_dimensions.rubric: States that the sixth independent fair flip is still 50/50 and cannot be predicted from the previous sequence.

tests.prompt: Name three Git commands for inspecting history. Output only a comma-separated list of exactly three command names, no explanations.

semantic_dimensions.name: git_validity
semantic_dimensions.rubric: All three items are real Git commands/subcommands useful for inspecting history, such as git log, git show, or git reflog.

tests.prompt: My program crashes. Tell me the exact line that is wrong.

semantic_dimensions.name: missing_context
semantic_dimensions.rubric: Does not fabricate a line number; clearly says the code/error context is missing and identifies the minimal information needed to diagnose it.

tests.prompt: A server's CPU is at 95%. Does that prove the application has a CPU bottleneck? Answer briefly and distinguish observation from conclusion.

semantic_dimensions.name: causal_caution
semantic_dimensions.rubric: States that high CPU utilization is evidence/observation but does not by itself prove an application CPU bottleneck; more profiling/context is needed.
